source.title: Train Flat, Then Compress: Sharpness-Aware Minimization Learns More Compressible Models
source.authors: Clara Na; Sanket Vaibhav Mehta; Emma Strubell

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper and appendix; no apparent truncation or garbling that blocks extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests flatness and compressibility in fine-tuned pretrained language models, a new setting relative to the mapped generalization-gap claim; it also measures sharpness but reports compression performance rather than the train–test gap.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for compression performance and sharpness, but does not measure training-versus-test error gaps or test whether networks that memorize random labels generalize on natural labels. Its compression and transfer results are related to the claim’s subject but do not measure any listed version. The paper’s generalization discussion cites prior work; those cited findings are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses prior flatness–generalization findings to motivate SAM-based compression of pretrained language models. Its own results measure compression performance, ticket transfer and sharpness, without testing any listed version. In particular, it does not relate magnitude-aware sharpness to train–test gaps (V7), and SAM uses Adam rather than providing an adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison (V4).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: SAM generally improves retained task performance under compression, and SAM-learned sparse structures tend to transfer better across tasks. The authors also report SWA comparisons, but regard the evidence across alternative flatness-inducing methods as insufficient for broad conclusions about flat minima generally.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tunes pretrained BERT variants on English NLP tasks, then compares compression outcomes under Adam, SAM, and in some settings SWA; evaluates compression robustness and sharpness rather than the mapped train–test generalization-gap claims.
record.method_sensitivity: Compression results vary with pruning method, sparsity, task, model variant, and whether ticket structure or final optimizer is varied. The authors report an exception for RoBERTabase on MRPC; RTE and SST-2 can have pruned-model accuracy above the full fine-tuned model.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM generally improves retained task performance after pruning or quantization, and SAM-derived sparse tickets tend to transfer better across tasks. These are compression and transfer comparisons rather than measurements of a listed claim.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM fine-tuning often improves compressibility and sparse-ticket transfer in the tested pretrained BERT variants and English NLP tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 3–4 report magnitude-aware sharpness, generally lower with SAM or SWA but with exceptions depending on task and perturbation radius. No corresponding train–test gaps or ranking analysis are reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM and SWA often yield lower measured sharpness than vanilla Adam in these fine-tuned BERT settings.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Evidence concerns task-specific compression performance in pretrained BERT variants on English sentence classification and question answering, not train–test error gaps. Many findings are plotted; some comparisons have limited seeds (often n = 3). The authors note substantial compute requirements, lack of behavioral evaluation beyond limited preliminary observations, and that they refrain from strong claims about flat minima generally because alternative flatness methods were not explored comprehensively.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were eligible: reported compression metrics and sharpness measurements do not measure the behavior named by any version. Cited prior generalization findings were excluded. Figure 16 reports Checklist behavior shifts under pruning but does not compare the mapped claim’s train–test gap or any version’s named behavior.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label generalization using the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Effects of adding or removing dropout on held-out error.
Association between magnitude-aware sharpness and train–test gaps at similarly low training loss, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T3 classification to uses_without_test/T4. Keeping eligible rows and verdicts empty is appropriate; the related compression and sharpness results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance under tuning conditions.
Large-batch effects on held-out performance under epoch budgets.
Whether magnitude-aware sharpness ranks train–test gaps.
Removal of memorized examples and its effect on test accuracy.
